### Service-directory commissioning and referral destinations

A directory maintainer needs to turn a changing list of organisations, services, locations, eligibility rules and opening times into a usable referral destination. The implementation payer commissions that integration; the directory publisher owns the source and its reuse terms; the referral team reviews the appropriate service; and the receiving engineer operates the installed application. The delivered Human Services Directory product connects those roles to the existing Gravity referral workflow.

**The operating journey.** Staff import the original HSDS JSON, CSV tables or archive, FHIR resources or retained provider capture. Each source keeps its publisher, original file, snapshot or incremental scope, complete records and relationships. Staff freeze an edition, inspect changed and unresolved identities against its predecessor, and review the full source-to-FHIR mapping. The saved service choice carries the original candidate list, eligibility, capacity and schedule interpretation. It distinguishes operating hours, events and exclusions and preserves supplied zero and null values. An explicit join binds that selected service to the original Gravity Task and ServiceRequest. The receiving engineer opens the complete editable directory and referral package, including earlier editions and the decisions used to select the destination. The [operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/products/human-services-directory/OPERATING.md) gives the native, browser, connected and installed workflow.

**Delivered source and current operation.** Merchant [PR402](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/402) and public [PR2444](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2444) / [PR2456](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2456) contain the complete source engine, mapping and referral domain, industrial operator, typed SDK, Merchant tools, Applications contribution and installation selection. The retained publisher basis contains 85 original Open Referral HSDS 3.3.1 files and 20 original HL7 Human Services Directory STU1 files. HSD's published mapping targets HSDS 2.0.1 and FHIR 4.0.1; the product exposes the 3.x migration decisions for review. The completed source operation imported all 24 original CSV tables plus nested JSON, indexed 65 rows and retained 86 relationship observations, including ambiguous and unresolved candidates. An edited service description produced one changed record and 23 unchanged records against the original CSV edition. Its FHIR source leg retained the complete 39-resource published eLTSS Bundle, including 98 resolved and two unresolved references. The [source notice](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fhir_directory/SOURCE_NOTICE.md) preserves attribution, and the [complete receiving programme](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/products/human-services-directory/RECEIVING.md) continues through selection, the original referral, handoff, browser, connected operation and installed receiving.

**Completed directory-to-referral receiving.** The original native operation completed on October 12 at 22:08 UTC. Its authored mapping carried twenty fields from three original rows into three FHIR resources, with zero errors and five retained warnings. The selected service kept its `criteria-not-met` classification and named follow-up owner. Its explicit referral join added those three directory resources, retained one binding and one clinical-field edit, and kept the complete seven-Task referral case. Independent receivers reopened the full editable workspace, selected-service handoff and final reviewed package with the same directory identity and original service reference. The complete editable result is 28,828,941 bytes and includes the source editions, mappings, selections, referral join and review history. The operation uses the unchanged published directory examples and explicitly authored decisions, with the original operated Gravity clinical examples.

**Repeatable work and declared relationships.** The merged [Directory Operating Plans](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/895) bind a customer's named task, source edition, owner, ordered work and destination to the same application. Staff can revise the procedure, export readable and editable handover, and receive its history with the whole workspace. The published recurring-edition programme retains the initial and refreshed directory, selected service and full receiving output; its authored description change preserves the other original records. These provide a concrete starting point for the next publisher refresh and the receiving engineer's repeated task.

The merged [declared-relationship engine](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/911) reads the original HSDS 3.3.1 declarations across twenty-four tables. It retains each source row, target candidate and exact match, so an existing relationship and an unambiguous destination remain separate findings. A selected empty target table produces a missing-target result; a table outside the selected edition keeps its unavailable coverage. The [operator, typed SDK, Merchant tools and CLI](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/944) expose every result page, original-row drill-down and all four complete relationship files. The complete native-to-customer receiving programme is published with these components; its next execution will exercise the eight retained source selections through browser, Merchant close/reopen and independent customer restoration.

**Staff corrections tied to the original edition.** The merged [source-correction workbench](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1081) lets an operator prepare changes to complete nested JSON objects, individual physical CSV cells or a whole ordered CSV row. A candidate preview retains the original source, the proposed values, the complete comparison and unchanged data. The operator accepts the reviewed candidate as a new edition; previous editions and source files remain available. The complete correction programme includes source preservation, conformance reassessment, browser and Merchant operation, and independent customer receiving. Its delivery recovery retains complete local work when a Save is interrupted and distinguishes execution from successful delivery.

**A complete customer correction round.** The merged [customer worksheet implementation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1171), also delivered in [public source](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/3185), carries selected original directory rows into an offline customer package. The customer sees the original values, proposes a complete JSON object or ordered CSV cells, and records a reason. The receiving operator retains the unchanged returned file, compares each typed change, and explicitly accepts it or keeps the original with a separate review reason. Missing fields, explicit nulls, numeric spelling, complete arrays and CSV cell positions keep their original meaning. Accepted decisions prepare the existing correction plan for its separate preview and acceptance. An all-kept review remains a complete result with no artificial correction. A later round can start from the accepted edition while retaining the earlier worksheet and decisions.

**Delivered interfaces and operating evidence.** The [maintained worksheet guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/305d54e216ad30705dcc6435e8ca41620090b164/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fhir_directory/CORRECTION_WORKSHEETS.md) covers the operator, offline customer editor, native CLI, typed SDK and Merchant tools. Whole source files, worksheet packages, returned bytes, comparisons and decisions travel with the editable workspace. Both product editions retain the complete implementation, with exact source readback and semantic review. The whole worksheet receiving programme starts from the already completed original Directory result and packet, then exercises two authored correction rounds, exact request reuse, the actual customer editor and independent customer restoration. Publication is complete; this new worksheet programme has not yet produced an observed completed native or browser result. Its authored return is an operating example, and no external customer acceptance is inferred.

**Customer returns against a later edition.** A directory may advance while a customer is reviewing an earlier worksheet. The merged [current-edition reconciliation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1234), also published in [the public product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/3293), lets staff select the actual current edition and explicitly match every original worksheet row to its current source record, with a reason. A row without a defensible match stays explicitly unbound. The review retains the original value, the customer's proposal and the current value separately. It distinguishes a clean proposal, an already-applied change, a conflict and a changed row structure, including the difference between a missing field and an explicit null.

**Explicit decisions and separate acceptance.** Staff decide every returned change: accept the proposal, keep the current value, or resolve the complete current row. A complete-row resolution retains the full JSON object or ordered CSV cells and requires consistent decisions for every change on that row; the product does not combine overlapping whole-row and field edits. The resulting ordinary correction plan is bound to the selected current edition. Preview and acceptance remain separate actions, and an all-kept review retains its complete decisions without creating an empty plan. The [maintained reconciliation guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e963db6a3cc2c29f4593c60e4084e670105bb7fb/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fhir_directory/WORKSHEET_RECONCILIATION.md) covers the operator, typed SDK, Merchant tools and native interfaces. Original worksheet and return bytes, row matches, comparisons, decisions, prior editions and accepted corrections travel together in the editable workspace.

**Complete receiving and current evidence.** Both product editions have merged the complete 32-file implementation, with all 64 source bodies read back exactly. The final saved-draft recovery successor is also merged in [the public product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/3367) and [Merchant](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1280), with all four updated file bodies read back. The whole reconciliation receiving programme composes the full 354-file application from retained source. It starts with the already completed original Directory result and packet, operates the worksheet prerequisite and current-edition review, and then continues through the actual offline customer editor, operator and Merchant, followed by an independent customer workspace. Each completed native stage is saved before browser work. The final customer packet is produced from the independently received state. One corrected admission verified its source helpers and began receiving the complete input before transport was lost. A later continuation lost transport before returning startup output; both handles reconciled as Unknown, which does not prove termination. The original operation's process, source intake and product lock require reconciliation before another continuation. Completed native, browser and customer outputs remain pending. The earlier intake stopped during source parsing before any workspace opened; its input and failure are retained. The authored customer proposals remain operating examples, and no external customer acceptance is inferred. This extends the existing commissioned correction round and receiving handover within the unchanged $38,000 / 400-hour / 150-day programme and six package allocations.

**Commissioning use within the existing terms.** This supplies the reviewable correction round already included in the Storm implementation offer and a concrete handover task for another commissioned directory installation. The source publisher and customer still select the actual records, permitted reuse and named review owner. The existing $38,000 / 400-hour / 150-day application and its six package allocations remain unchanged. Source and staff-role integration belongs to the existing T1 scope, paid operation and interrupted delivery to T2, and recurring customer use and receiving handover to T3. Each commissioned adaptation is assigned once through its original workorder; this reusable capability adds no budget line or new award claim.

**A saved service choice reviewed against a later source.** A referral team can retain a justified service choice while the publisher releases a different edition. The merged [complete saved-choice refresh](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/2026) now makes that next operating decision explicit in the same Directory. Staff select the original saved choice and the actual later source edition, then bind each original candidate to one unique current service or record a reasoned omission. A missing candidate is shown with the selected edition's source coverage; it is not described as a closure or proof of unavailability. Two old candidates cannot silently collapse onto one new service.

The review keeps the full original and current service objects, eligibility criteria, locations, schedules, supplied capacities and contact context. Staff record every current candidate's disposition and reason; a reserve or needs-contact decision retains its follow-up owner. A later location or schedule must belong to the explicitly selected current edition. Missing fields, explicit nulls, supplied zero and original lexical values remain distinguishable. The original evaluator determines the successor's complete classification; the refresh does not override it or promise that a place is available.

**A prepared report followed by a separate decision.** Preparing a refresh retains its complete input, original selection, later source, row bindings, proposed choice, comparisons and seven downloadable files: Input.json, Refresh.json, Proposed_Selection.json, Service_Choices.csv, Criteria.csv, START_HERE.html and Service_Choice_Refresh.zip. Staff inspect that immutable report before accepting its exact SHA-256 with a named actor and note. Acceptance uses the ordinary selection writer and retains the original predecessor and refresh ID. Repeating that same acceptance returns the same successor. Earlier choices remain intact; the operation does not alter clinical/referral records, provider data or source editions.

The successor's ordinary customer handoff includes the full review archive and readable link, so the next operator can inspect why the chosen service changed and which contact question remains open. Full editable export/receiving carries the old and new selections, all source editions, complete reviews and accepted relationship. The [complete operating and receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/a7da1391088377556d9126eaabac1e5a87eeeb90/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fhir_directory/SELECTION_REFRESH.md) exposes the same browser, native CLI, typed client and Merchant actions, plus a same-Workspace export and cold-reopen continuation. This supplies a concrete recurring directory-refresh task within the existing commissioned workorder, not a new budget line, purchase event or referral authority.

**Current implementation and evidence boundary.** Merchant PR2026 is merged at `a7da1391088377556d9126eaabac1e5a87eeeb90`. All twenty-two complete changed source bodies and the committed full postimage/preimage capsule were independently read back; the backend, typed actions and browser/native call paths received focused source review. The current source consists of 645,682 bytes across those twenty-two files. These are implementation and source results. The original 450E receiving operation and Workspace `2c51f522-4852-463b-bdc0-59389d7bae83` remain selected for actual native, browser and attachment use; no completed new execution, external customer acceptance, availability confirmation or payment is inferred. **The useful Stellar service.** A commissioned merchant can offer one authorised directory edition, one complete reviewed service-selection result, or an agreed refresh and change report. Its workorder fixes the source edition, complete output, priced unit, receiving application and event that makes a later purchase useful. A new published edition, changed service availability or a distinct customer query can supply that later task. The buyer approves the selected asset, amount and request through the existing merchant/buyer flow. The native facilitator delegates verification and settlement to the official Stellar x402 SDK; the acquired result then enters the directory application with its original source and selection. The application retains full directory and referral data in the selected operator workspace. The network transaction pays for the agreed service. The [native merchant and facilitator](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/native-facilitator/README.md) provide the payment implementation, while the existing application payment register supplies the actual purchase history.

**Commissioning within the funded programme.** This is a source-specific implementation option inside the existing two-merchant/two-buyer, $38,000 / 400-hour / 150-day plan. The completed reusable product is the starting point. T1's existing 80-hour resource integration and 40-hour authority/handover packages connect the selected publisher, actual service output and independent receiving operator to that customer's application. T2's existing 70-hour provider deployment and 50-hour response packages operate the same paid result through both facilitators and recover interrupted payment/delivery cases. T3's existing 90-hour mainnet rollout and 70-hour recovery/handover packages carry recurring useful purchases, the original service history and a complete receiving-host restoration. The programme's existing cohort targets apply across the selected installations. The commissioned workorder assigns each actual adaptation once, with source access, deployment charges, staff participation and customer acceptance attached to its original owner.

**Concrete commissioning offer.** On October 13, the original company operation sent Storm Consultancy a £9,600 workshare, covering 128 planned hours over twenty business days, with three £3,200 milestones. The proposed scope is one source family and receiving application, three editions, up to 5,000 services and 50,000 rows, one correction round and four staff hours. Storm retains its customer relationship; the workshare provides the agreed source intake, mapping, edition comparison and complete operator handover. Its original source and offered terms remain with that company case. This gives the existing grant programme a specific agency commissioning route, while the selected merchant, independent buyer and useful paid service are assigned through the original installation workorder.

The independently usable result is a selected service and referral that the next operator can understand, update and continue. Source refresh, mapping correction, changed availability and receiving-host restoration use the retained application history. The [product source and entry points](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/products/human-services-directory/README.md) and the original SCF delivery give the complete maintained installation.

# Receive Human Services Directory into the existing grant assembly

This contribution receives the complete Directory customer journey and twenty measured source registrations through the original application composer. It owns the existing **Service-directory commissioning and referral destinations** H3 inside **Referral implementation: source changes, returned outcomes and complete receiving**. The original cumulative publisher retains the saved application, review, Page and Site.

## Complete maintained inputs

- `products/human-services-directory/GRANT.md`: the complete customer chapter, including the original completed Directory receiving, standards and relationships, staff corrections, offline customer worksheets and returned work against a later accepted edition.
- `products/human-services-directory/GRANT_EVIDENCE.json`: original completed native result and full editable-packet identities, nineteen measured product sources and the distinct status of the newer whole programme.
- `stellar-forge/developer-site/grant-products/human-services-directory.json`: the twenty-source declaration under the existing Referral H2.
- `stellar-forge/developer-site/grant-directory.mjs`: a source-only receiving helper that replaces exactly the selected Directory H3 and verifies the current complete subsection digest. Its whole prefix and suffix remain byte-identical.
- This complete receiving guide.

The current product source is Merchant reconciliation merge `7fcf609e926d26e353954fc1a1527f4fbbc65010` followed by saved-draft recovery merge `e963db6a3cc2c29f4593c60e4084e670105bb7fb`. Corresponding public merges are `ffe2bf91f780c5873af78499c4df641ecd9641fa` and `c15780c96cc7ea40792d2c700b3410baf30f11d1`. The declaration measures the complete actual selected file bodies, including the current guide, engine, typed client, tool catalogue, Applications bridge, distribution selection and native/browser/customer courses.

Start with the cumulative publisher's current full source and current full manuscript. Preserve every newer peer contribution. For the explicitly retained PR1286 companion this is `8a4acd8a948f870d7dcaa094c14052a8149a6b85839121995e7436ed3eea15c7`; a later source is reviewed and measured in its own right.

node stellar-forge/developer-site/grant-directory.mjs \
  --manuscript /private/scf/current-complete-manuscript.md \
